body:
Apache / PHP.
And there is a known behaviour about string comparison which is case-sensitive especially with the [apache_request_headers](http://php.net/manual/fr/function.apache-request-headers.php) method.
Full discussion is [here](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/5258977/are-http-headers-case-sensitive).

In anyway, this is not the concern of the client.
I hope you get the point @vicb .

The point I get is that this is a bug in Apache and you should create a ticket there.
We conform to the spec they don't. And that's exactly what your link is about, nothing else.

That being said I'll check what we can do on our side to mitigate the Apache bug.

It would help if you can find a precise description of the Apache bug. Thanks.

I agree with @vicb that the root cause is in the server if it doesn't follow spec. Having said this I'm not sure we need / should be touching headers for the outgoing requests. We should retrieve _response_ headers in the case-insensitive way but I don't think we've got much business in touching casing of request headers.

This is all grey area of course but we might be on a slightly safer side if we don't mess with request headers.

**The fact**
Specifications are: "Field names are case-insensitive.".

**My understanding**
It does not mean "normalize".
It does mean "do not consider the case".

**The use-case**
If client wants to send "Authentication", "aUtHeNtICaTiOn", "AUTHENTICATION", ... he must be able to send it as he wants.
A bug-free server will basically consider all of it as equivalent to "authentication".

**The conclusion**
This is not to a third-part client to decide that.

@vicb with

```
headers.set('content-type', v1);
headers.set('Content-Type', v2);
```

the result should be:

```
headers.get('CONTENT-TYPE') == v2
```

Client frameworks SHOULD NOT change the case of headers; and if a framework sets the header, the framework SHOULD use the canonical representation of the header name (`Content-Type` in this case) as [maintained by IANA](http://www.iana.org/assignments/message-headers/message-headers.xml#perm-headers): `Content-Type        http    standard    [RFC7231, Section 3.1.1.5]`.

[RFC7231, Section 3.1.1.5](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-3.1.1.5):

```
3.1.1.5.  Content-Type

   The "Content-Type" header field indicates the media type of the
   associated representation: either the representation enclosed in the
   message payload or the selected representation, as determined by the
   message semantics.  The indicated media type defines both the data
   format and how that data is intended to be processed by a recipient,
   within the scope of the received message semantics, after any content
   codings indicated by Content-Encoding are decoded.

     Content-Type = media-type
```

**Current behavior** 

<!-- Describe how the bug manifests. -->

The Header class in the Http bundle uses the normalize function to normalize the header key, before adding the header key value pair to the header. In chrome the normalize function always transforms the header key to lower case. However, in the header we almost always want the first letter of the header key to be upper case.
**Expected behavior**

<!-- Describe what the behavior would be without the bug. -->

Make sure, that the header key is not modified.
